newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Workers protest near ailing Portuguese copper firm.
newsitem.headline: Workers protest near ailing Portuguese copper firm.

text.p: About 80 workers staged a protest outside the factory of ailing Portuguese copper company Companhia Portuguesa do Cobre (CPC) in the northern city of Oporto on Friday to demand payment of wage arrears.
"We are four months behind on our wages. We are demanding payment of at least one month of our wage arrears for now," CPC employee Jorge Dias told TSF radio outside the factory.
Workers held a similar protest on Wednesday, blocking traffic to press demands for payment of wage arrears.
The company, which employs 250 people, is in severe financial difficulties and now operates at just 25 percent capacity, its director Figueiroa Goncalves said on Thursday.

CPC was depending on the so-called Mateus Plan, a recent initiative named after Economy Minister Augusto Mateus, to help it recover from its problems with the support of bank financing backed by state guarantees.

The annual turnover of CPC, which processes copper, aluminium and brass mainly for domestic industry including state utility EDP-Electricidade de Portugal, has plunged in recent years to around two billion escudos ($12 million), Goncalves said. $1=163.5 escudos
